Measured instance from #2412's Step 10d gate (2026-08-20), added as evidence rather than filing a
duplicate (workflow-fix dedup on target_file + fingerprint; this task owns the fence).

**Observed:** the Step 10d pre-push lint gate returned verdict `crash` with
`BASE_RC=124 GATED_RC=124` — both leg PAIRS killed by their 900 s `timeout` wrapper.

**Which leg, specifically:** each pair is two invocations appending to one file. Leg 1 (no-flags
default run, measured ~4.5-6 min) COMPLETED and PASSED on both baseline and gated sides — both files
are complete at 2,900 bytes / 25 lines ending in `workflow_lint: PASS`, with the expected
size-check WARNs. The 124 came from **leg 2**, the parity invocation
`--check-references --check-tables --check-asks --check-autonomous-asks`, which the recipe itself
measures at **~1.4 s** idle. It was killed with zero output.

**Why that sharpens the fence-sizing case:** this is not the slow leg exceeding a tight bound. It is
a SECOND-SCALE leg hitting a 900 s wall — a ~640x blowup that fleet CPU contention does not plausibly
explain. The likelier mechanism is `uv run` blocking on uv-cache lock contention with concurrent
gates (two foreign gates were live; the run had been launched fail-open at the gate-fleet cap
expiry). Because `timeout` wraps the whole `uv run python ...` invocation, time spent blocked
acquiring a lock is charged against the leg's wall. So the fence is not merely sized off the idle
range — it is sized off *compute* wall while bounding an invocation whose wall can be dominated by
LOCK WAIT.

**Consequence for the gate's own contract:** the crash arm then fails CLOSED on a run whose
substantive lint comparison was clean (`lint-new` and `lint-owndiff` both 0 bytes,
baseline-norm == gated-norm), costing a full ~35 min gate cycle plus a fresh queue wait. Failing
closed is correct — the parity-leg checks genuinely did not run — but the trigger was a lock wait,
not a lint problem.

**Possible directions (for this task's own plan to weigh, not decided here):** size the per-leg fence
off the LOADED range; or bound compute rather than wall; or serialize `uv run` across concurrent
gates; or split the fence per leg so the ~1.4 s parity leg does not inherit the slow leg's 900 s
bound. Not fixed from #2412 — unilaterally widening a fence to get one's own merge through is the
banned shape.

[cross-task] The FENCE half of this task's ask landed in #2253 round 5. Remaining scope narrows to verdict legibility. Status left at `proposed` — no automation flips classification, and the surviving half still needs dispatch.

## What landed (not here — in #2253)

#2253 (`kind: infra`, the `workflow_lint` production-import-resolvability check) hit exactly the incident this task predicts: its Step 10d pre-push gate returned `crash` with `GATED_RC = BASE_RC = 124`, both no-flags lint legs killed by the 900 s per-leg fence. Commit `9b8c59502219bb8c116cdbd97525b65ac9171397` on branch `issue-2253` raises the fence at all **8** sites in `.claude/skills/issue/steps/18-step-10d.md` from `900s` to `1800s` (`--kill-after=60s` unchanged; TG legs untouched — they are sized from the selector's own `recommended-timeout-s`).

**Re-derived from the LOADED range, with the arithmetic written next to the constant** — this task's primary acceptance criterion. Measured 2026-08-21 in the issue-2253 worktree at the production entrypoint under fleet load (load avg 13.44 / 32 cores, 9 concurrent `workflow_lint.py` processes):

| leg | wall |
|---|---|
| no-flags full bundle | **747 s** |
| parity leg (`--check-references --check-tables --check-asks --check-autonomous-asks`) | **2 s** |
| the #2253 check alone | 84 s |
| fixed startup floor | 1 s |

`1800 s ≥ 2 × 747 s` satisfies the CLAUDE.md ×2 dispersion default. The stale first-site comment (which sized the fence as "≈ 2.5× the measured 360 s upper wall") is replaced by that measured basis plus the rc-124→crash-arm consequence, so the next reader can check the arithmetic rather than re-derive it.

**Durability pin:** `tests/test_issue_skill_gate_leg_timeout_floor.py` enforces a ≥1500 s floor on every `workflow_lint`-wrapping leg bound in that doc, with a ≥8-leg anchor assertion so a reshaped invocation fails loud instead of silently escaping the floor. Teeth proven against the pre-fix content: parsed `[900] × 8` → `AssertionError: bound 900s < floor 1500s`. `tests/test_step10d_guard3.py:1112/1115` pinned the `900s` literal directly and moved to `1800s` in the same commit (shipping a knowingly-red pin would have failed the very gate the round unblocks).

## This task's framing was right, and sharper than the one I reached independently

I first read the defect as a correctly-sized fence that went stale as the linter grew. That is WRONG, and this task has it right: 900 s is ~2.5× the **idle** 4.5-6 min figure, i.e. sized off precisely the range the same subsection forbids ("Size any wall-time-derived fence off the LOADED range, not the idle one"). The 747 s loaded measurement and the ~360 s idle upper wall are consistent simultaneously — ~2× contention slowdown with 9 concurrent lints — so the linter did not grow; the fence was mis-sized against idle from the start. Correcting the record because the two readings imply different fixes: "went stale" suggests a re-measure cadence, whereas the real defect was an instruction/implementation contradiction inside one subsection, which is what the floor pin now prevents from recurring.

Independent corroboration of the contention story from #2253's incident: the BASELINE leg runs `origin/main`'s own lint on a pristine main tree — no payload at all — and was killed the same way, and the SAME payload at the SAME fence passed both leg pairs on an earlier run hours before (provable, not inferred: a `block` verdict is only reachable when the crash arm is false, which requires `GATED_RC ≤ 1` and `BASE_RC ≤ 1`, and a killed leg yields 124).

## What does NOT land — the surviving ask

The **verdict-legibility** half is untouched and remains this task's scope: a contention timeout still lands in the same `crash` bucket as a genuine linter crash, whose prescribed recovery is "fix the crash cause in the worktree" — which sends the reader hunting a defect that does not exist.

Confirmed while diagnosing #2253: there is **no** `[diag] verdict inputs` line anywhere in the current spec (zero hits in `18-step-10d.md` at repo root AND on the issue-2253 branch), so the #2204 report that quotes one was reading a locally-modified script instance, not the shipped recipe. Nothing in the shipped gate exposes `GT_RC` / `BASE_RC` / `GATED_RC` / `TG_CRASH` / `TG_RC` / `TG_BASE_RC`. Diagnosing which of the six crash arms fired on #2253 therefore took a reverse-engineering chain — counting verdict lines per leg capture, proving from the argparse `no_flags` expression which leg emits the conflict-markers line, then closing the timing arithmetic with a separately measured 2 s parity wall. That cost is exactly what this half exists to remove, and it recurs for every future reader.

Deliberately NOT folded into #2253 r5, for reasons that are about correctness rather than convenience: (a) it is not required for that round's merge — the fence raise is; (b) changing the verdict WORD would alter the gate's public contract, which is not a change to make as a side effect of an unrelated round; and (c) adding emitted output perturbs the `test_step10d_guard3.py` command-line-count pins that r5 already had to adjust, so it wants its own review round rather than riding along.

Suggested shape for whoever picks this up: emit the six rc inputs on one line before the verdict block (cheap, no contract change, would have collapsed the whole chain above to one read), and consider a distinct verdict word or a crash-arm annotation so the recovery instruction can branch on contention-vs-crash instead of conflating them.

Additional fence site for this task's audit list — surfaced from #2273 (kind: infra, doc-only gotchas.md entry), 2026-08-22

WHO/WHERE: posted by the autonomous /issue 2273 session while its Step 9c gate ran. FYI + scope
addition for #2409; nothing is blocked on it and no action is needed from anyone right now.
#2409 is still at `proposed`, so this lands before planning and costs nothing to absorb.

THE ADDITION. This task's acceptance criteria already require the same treatment for "the sibling
fences in the same gate: the mapped-baseline leg (5040s), the gated TG leg (4620s), and the Step 9c
gate's recommended_timeout_s()". That list is missing one site, on a DIFFERENT file:

    .claude/agents/code-reviewer.md:1155
    timeout --kill-after=30s 540s uv run python scripts/workflow_lint.py \
      > /tmp/reviewer-lint-<N>.txt 2>&1; echo "no-flags lint rc=$?"

This is the review-time no-flags lint leg added by #1805. It runs the SAME instrument this task is
re-sizing — its own comment says so ("the same instrument as the Step 10d gate's lint leg") — at a
**540s** fence, while the eight Step 10d invocations of that instrument
(.claude/skills/issue/steps/18-step-10d.md:1207/1210/1348/1351/3814/3817/3920/3923) use **1800s**.
One instrument, two sites, a 3.3x fence disparity, and the tighter one sits at the review site.

WHY IT MATCHES THIS TASK'S FINGERPRINT RATHER THAN BEING ITS OWN TASK. Against this task's own
measured figures — ~4.5-6 min no-flags on an IDLE VM, 30-40 min under typical fleet load with 3+
concurrent gates — 540s is roughly 1.5-2x the IDLE no-flags wall and far below the LOADED one. That
is precisely the "sized off the IDLE range the same section forbids" defect, and it inherits the
same second-order cost: a `rc=124` here surfaces to the reviewer as a lint result, so a fleet-load
timeout can present as a lint finding on the round's payload. Same fingerprint, same instrument,
different file — hence a scope addition here rather than a duplicate task.

TRIGGER SCOPE (stated so the audit is not over-sold). The leg is NARROW: it fires only when the
diff ADDS a scripts/ or src/ *.py file (`--diff-filter=A`, #1805). It therefore does NOT fire on
doc-only rounds — it did not fire on #2273 — so this is a latent mis-sizing that bites only rounds
adding a new script, not an every-round breakage. That is also why it has stayed invisible.

CORROBORATING OBSERVATIONS, with their provenance, all LOADED-range (none is a clean idle
measurement, and none should be used as the fence basis — this task's own idle/loaded pair should):
- #2273's Step 9c gate, running while this note was written, spent >10 min inside the single node
  `tests/test_workflow_lint.py::test_workflow_lint_default_exits_zero` — the no-flags lint as a
  test — under heavy contention (the gate saturated the shared cores enough to background an
  unrelated grep). Wall at observation: 32m34s, gate at 86%.
- #2273's round-1/round-2 reviewers each attempted a full no-flags lint at self-chosen 590/570/540s
  fences and all three returned INCONCLUSIVE, falling back to targeted --check-* legs. Note this
  was NOT the spec leg above (the #1805 trigger was false for a doc-only diff) — it is evidence
  about the wall, not about this spec site.
- #2235 (completed) measured the inline payload lint gate at 9m08s, and records that dropping every
  hygiene check still leaves a ~7 min gate. Different gate, wider scope than the no-flags leg
  alone, so it bounds the instrument's cost from above rather than giving the leg's own wall.

SUGGESTED MINIMAL RESOLUTION (this task's call, not a prescription): fold code-reviewer.md:1155
into the same re-derivation, so one arithmetic covers every site running this instrument; and if
the reviewer-side leg is deliberately meant to stay tighter than the gate's, say so next to the
number with the reason, since the present disparity reads as drift rather than intent.

A SECOND, SMALLER GAP — probably out of scope here, recorded so it is not lost. Nothing tells a
reviewer what to do when the #1805 trigger is FALSE but it wants a full-run lint verdict anyway
(e.g. to check an acceptance criterion phrased as "no new no-flags lint failure"). #2273's three
reviewers each improvised a fence, each blew it, and each reported INCONCLUSIVE — so a criterion
of that shape is currently unverifiable at the review site. The fix is prose, not a fence
(either give reviewers the measured wall so they can size one, or tell them to route that
verification to the Step 9c / Step 10d gate and report deferral instead of attempting it). Split
this out as its own task if #2409 stays fence-arithmetic-only.
